summary: Each turn you roll six dice Yahtzee-style, re-rolling to chase claws (attack), hearts (heal), energy, or victory points, while whoever is inside Tokyo takes damage from everyone else's attacks but can't heal. It's a fast, loud, push-your-luck brawl where you're constantly deciding whether to stay in the punishing but point-rich city or retreat to safety.
praised: extremely easy to teach and fast to play
fun monster theme and card powers
criticised: heavy luck can make outcomes feel arbitrary
player elimination can leave people sitting out
little strategic depth beyond dice math
runaway leader problem if someone gets a strong card engine

interaction.detail: Attacks from the player in Tokyo hit everyone else simultaneously, and everyone else's attacks hit whoever is in Tokyo, so the shared 'who occupies Tokyo' state is the main lever players fight over. There's no private tableau of real consequence beyond your own health and cards; the board state is almost entirely shared and adversarial.

scoring.why: The game ends the instant someone hits 20 victory points or is the last monster standing.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by racing to 20 victory points through dice rolls and Tokyo occupation, or by being the last monster left alive.
